summary: A Luminate analysis commissioned by TikTok finds that US TikTok users are much more likely than average consumers to pay for music streaming, buy merch, attend live shows, and discover and share music. The article ties this to TikTok's push into music services such as SoundOn and TikTok Music, while noting ongoing political risks over ByteDance and data concerns.
one_line: A TikTok-commissioned Luminate study finds 62% of US TikTok users pay for music streaming versus 43% of consumers, as TikTok expands in music.
key_facts: 62% of US TikTok users pay for a music streaming service, compared to 43% of all consumers, per a Luminate analysis commissioned by TikTok.
Luminate studied the US, UK, Germany, Brazil and Indonesia plus global data for July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2023.
TikTok had 150 million US users as of February 2023, implying about 93 million paying for a music streaming subscription.
In the US, 89% of TikTok users subscribed to at least one music streaming service versus 74% of overall consumers; in the UK it was 85% versus 62%.
In the US, 45% of TikTok users bought music-related merch over 12 months versus 35% of overall music listeners, and 38% attended a live music event versus 33%.
US TikTok users spent 22% more on music-related purchases than overall music listeners.
TikTok users were 108% more likely to discover and share music than other social media users in the UK, 100% in Germany and 71% in the US.
The report says TikTok users prefer international music more than average listeners, helping launch global artists in Reggaeton, Afrobeats and K-Pop.
TikTok launched SoundOn, a music distribution service, last year, partnered with TuneCore and FUGA.

TikTok Music, a premium-only streaming service, launched in summer 2023 in Brazil and Indonesia with all three major labels, then expanded to Australia, Mexico and Singapore without Universal's catalog.
In October, TikTok announced its first live music event 'TikTok In The Mix' and struck a deal with Distrokid for indie artists to upload to TikTok Music and Capcut.
TikTok unveiled an 'Add to Music App' feature to save music to Apple Music, Amazon Music or Spotify.
Governments from the US to the EU to Australia have banned TikTok from government devices; Montana and Nepal have banned or are moving to ban it altogether.
